current.text: He is a rookie. The Kings drafted him with the number 7 pick, and he is expected to start at point guard.
The projected Kings starters are Acuff, LaVine, Hunter, Murray and Sabonis, and nobody is pushing that group for a starting spot. The roster has no third point guard.
In Summer League he had 39% usage, 19 points and 4.5 assists, but shot 35% from the field, 27% from three and under 70% at the line. He took 29 shots in his first California Classic game.
He shares the ball with Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis, which should cut his usage.
He should have the ball in his hands and could be the 1A or primary scorer as a rookie. His upside depends on whether the Kings trade LaVine or Sabonis.
The Kings could still trade LaVine or Sabonis, which would open more usage for him.
Expected to score over 15 points a game but shoot under 40% from the field, with very poor shooting early in the season.

Experts disagree on his category-league price. One 9-cat mock takes him around pick 120. Another expert projects him outside the top 200 in categories and calls a 10th or 11th round pick reasonable mainly in points leagues.
Experts expect the Kings to finish near the bottom of the league.

durable.text: He is a high-usage, ball-dominant guard who should post good assist numbers and take many threes.
Most experts expect poor field goal shooting. They point to shot selection and trouble finishing at the rim, and call him the rookie most likely to hurt you with bad shooting.
Ham disagrees with that view. He says Acuff's efficiency and scoring are further along than De'Aaron Fox's were, and he expects a much better rookie year than Fox had.
He is a poor defender, so experts expect few steals and poor rebounding.
He is worth more in points leagues than in 9-cat category leagues.

note: He sits at the edge of our 144-player draft. Yahoo ranks him 127 at 2 USD and ESPN ranks him 138 at about 1.6 USD, so he is a last-dollar flyer at most. His projected 42.6% FG on about 14 shots a game and 2.5 turnovers only fit a team that can absorb FG% and TO in exchange for points and assists. Early in the season, check his FG%, his share of shots next to LaVine and Sabonis, and any trade of either one.
